punchline: ENIAC's programmers worked from wiring diagrams without ever seeing the machine at first, and at its 1946 debut the credit went to its builders.
thirty_sec: During the war, women at the Moore School calculated shell trajectories by hand. Six of them were picked to program ENIAC. With no manual, and at first no clearance to see the machine, they learned it from wiring diagrams. In February 1946 their trajectory program ran in front of reporters. The praise went to the engineers who built ENIAC, and the women were not named in the captions.
